subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & SLA targets (Aurora Health)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity & SLA targets (Aurora Health)

Thanks for taking the time today — really appreciate the candid discussion. Quick recap from our discovery call and the next steps we agreed on. Please reply with anything I missed.

Summary of pain / goals
- Primary pain: unpredictable latency and token costs from current multi-tenant endpoints for clinical summarization and patient triage models.
- Compliance/isolation: must run in a logically isolated reserved GPU pool due to PHI handling and SOC 2 requirements.
- Scale: need predictable throughput for daytime surge (8am–6pm) with bursts for batch jobs overnight.
- SLA goal: 99.9% availability for inference endpoints; P95 tail latency < 250ms for standard prompts.

Proposed dedicated capacity profile (high-level)
- Reserved: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved capacity) to start.
- Isolation: dedicated tenant with network controls + KMS-managed keys.
- Scaling: autoscale policy to add up to +50% burst capacity (pre-warmed GPUs) during peak windows.
- Onboarding: 4-week phased rollout (dev -> canary -> full prod).

Next steps / actions
1) We will share a preliminary RFQ and draft SLA for procurement (attached).
2) Ben to provide committed capacity pricing and billing cadence by EOD tomorrow.
3) Marissa (Solutions) & Rishi (SRE) will prepare the onboarding checklist and technical runbook.
4) Aurora to confirm procurement contacts and any internal timelines for approvals.

Planned timeline
- RFQ + draft SLA shared: 2027-05-11 (attached)
- Procurement Q&A / contract redline window: 1–2 weeks after RFQ
- Target onboarding start: ~4 weeks after contract execution

Attachments: Aurora_RFQ_Q2_2027.xlsx (xlsx, ~92KB), SLA_DRAFT_Aurora_2027.pdf (pdf, ~48KB)

Thanks — available for a quick follow-up if you want to walk through the RFQ.

Best,
Ben Carter

Hi Samantha (and procurement team),

Thanks — attaching the RFQ spreadsheet and draft SLA as discussed. Quick answers while you review:
- Pricing cadence: committed capacity pricing is quoted on an annual commitment with monthly invoicing; we can also provide a monthly-only option at a higher unit rate if you prefer no-term flexibility.
- 12-month illustrative pricing (committed 8 GPUs + projected burst):
   • Committed (8x reserved GPUs): $112,000/mo (equivalent to $1,344,000/yr) at enterprise committed discount (volume & term-dependent).
   • Estimated burst usage (on-demand for spikes): ~$18,000/mo (variable).
   • Typical onboarding credit: we can offer a one-time onboarding credit worth up to $25k (requires approval).
- SLA: draft included; standard SLA is 99.9% with credits for sustained monthly downtime. For custom SLA language (uptime windows, specific RTOs for model hotstart), we can negotiate.
- Security: we’ll provide a SOC 2 Type II package and the encryption/KMS architecture diagram once we have a DPA/NDA in place.

Onboarding plan (high level)
Week 1: Provision reserved GPU pool + network peering (dev).
Week 2: Model deployment + integration tests (canary users).
Week 3: Performance tuning, KV/prefix caching enabled, run smoke tests for latency/SLOs.
Week 4: Production cutoff and monitoring handoff; schedule weekly check-ins for first 6 weeks.

Action items
- Ben: Share RFQ + SLA (attached) — DONE.
- Procurement: Review RFQ and confirm procurement timelines / required PO process.
- Marissa & Rishi: Share technical runbook and onboarding checklist (Marissa, can you post that here or to the Drive link?).

Attachments: Aurora_RFQ_Q2_2027.xlsx, SLA_DRAFT_Aurora_2027.pdf

If procurement is ready, we can draft the contract and send a DocuSign link within 48 hours for a first-pass signature.

Best,

Thanks Sam — looping in the onboarding/runbook items as promised. High-level checklist (we'll share the full runbook on Drive):
- Network & security: VPC peering, allowed CIDR ranges, KMS key provisioning, and audit logging (we'll provide templates).
- Model ops: container packaging requirements, model artifact storage (S3/GCS), and KV cache warm-up guidance.
- Performance: target P95 <250ms; we'll run a canary at 10% traffic and then 50% before full cutover.
- Rollout: 2-week canary window recommended for clinical workloads.

DocuSign: Ben can send a first-pass MSA/Order Form; once procurement confirms redline windows we'll prepare the DocuSign envelope.
